sentences.text:
The petitioner has filed this petition being aggrieved by the arbitral award passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner/Arbitrator, Bengaluru Urban District, Bengaluru, in No.
LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR/14/2010-11 dated 18.12.2020 pertaining to Sy. No. 42 measuring 1100 Sq.
Meters (11 guntas) equivalent to 11836 Sq. feet of Sonnappanahalli village.
A.P. No.97/2021 .2.

The definite case of the petitioner is that the property measuring 1100 Sq.
Meters in Sy. No. 42 of Sonnappanahalli village has been acquired under Preliminary Notification issued by the respondent No. 3 under Section 3A(1) vide S.O. No.1270E) dated 05.12.2002 and Final Notification under Section 3D(1) and (2) vide S.O. No.829(E) dated 22.07.2003.
The respondent No.4 has passed the award on 21.01.2004 and determined the market value of agricultural lands at Rs. 4 lakhs per acre and that of NA lands at Rs. 45/- per Sq. feet.

The respondent No.4 awarded a total compensation amount of Rs.56,848/- in respect of 5.5 guntas of land each in Sy. No.42 to the respondents 1 and 2, which has been received by the respondent No.1 and 2 under protest.
Subsequently, on 22.07.2010 / 24.07.2010 the respondent No. 1 and 2 have filed an application for enhancing the compensation at the rate of Rs.1,00,00,000/- per Sq. acre.
Accordingly, the application is taken by the respondent No.3 for consideration.
. 3 . T h e r e a f t e r , t h e A r b i t r a t o r h o l d a n i n q u i r y a n d p a s s e d c o m m o n o r d e r i n LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR/14/2010-11 dated 18.12.2020.

Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioner filed this petition under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, setting aside the following:
:GROUNDS:
The petitioner claims that the impugned award passed by the respondent No.3 is perverse, patently illegal, capricious and goes against the fundamentals of Arbitration and Conciliation Act.
The impugned arbitral award is completely illegal and arbitrary and without according any reasons.

sentences.text: The respondent No.3 has not at all taken the trouble of independently conducting an inquiry into the market value of the subject lands as on the date of Preliminary Notification and the respondent No.3 has given the benefit of enhancement to the respondent No. 1 & 2 without production of any documentary or oral evidence by the respondent No. 1 & 2.

It is also claimed by the petitioner that the respondent No. 3 A.P. No.97/2021 placing reliance upon notification dated 21.07.2004 fixed the guidance value of NA lands is Rs. 60/- per Sq.
feet but such notification not produced and that is not part of records.

Further it is claimed that the respondent No. 3 exorbitantly enhanced the market value without any reason and considered subsequent market value than the market value of the date of preliminary notification and among grounds, prayed for relief claimed in the petition.
.5. The respondent No. 1 to 4 though served with the notice, not chosen to appear before this Court to resist the petition and hence, they were placed exparte.
The entire records in LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR/14/2010-11 secured from the Arbitrator.

.6. On the basis of above, the points for consideration are as under:
1) Whether the impugned award of the Arbitrator/SLAO is against law, fact, evidence and probabilities of the case and liable to be intervened by this Court?
2) What order or award?
.7. Heard the arguments.

The petitioner has produced the citations i.e., (1) Oil and Natural Gas Corp. Ltd Vs. SAW Pipes (AIR A.P. No.97/2021 2003 SC 2629); (2) Ssangyong Engineering &

REASONS .8. POINT No.1:
Before proceeding further in this case, it is relevant to note admitted and undisputed facts in this case.

The respondent No.1 and 2 are the owners of the land in Sy. No.42 measuring to an extent of 1100 Sq. Meters (11 guntas)
equivalent to 11836 Sq. feet situated at Sonnappanahalli village and the said property has been acquired for widening of NH-7 under Preliminary Notification dated 05.12.2002 and Final Notification dated 22.07.2003
is an admitted fact.

It is also an admitted and undisputed fact in this case that the respondent No.4/Special Land Acquisition and Competent Authority of National Highways Authority of India being a SLAO determined the compensation at A.P. No.97/2021 Rs.4,00,000/- per Sq. acre and that of NA lands at Rs. 45/- per Sq.

sentences.text: It is also admitted and undisputed fact that awarded compensation has been disbursed to the respondent No. 1 and 2 as compensation.

.9. Subsequent to the receipt of compensation or passing of the award, the respondent No. 1 and 2 filed an application before the respondent No. 3 claiming that they are entitled for compensation at the rate of Rs.5,00,000/-per acre.
On the basis of the said application, the respondent No.3 hold an inquiry and passed order in LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR/14/2010-11 dated 10.10.2023.

The respondent No.
3 has held that the guidance value of agricultural lands situated at Sonnappanahalli village was Rs.
60/- per Sq. feet and added 75% on the guidance value i.e., Rs. 45/- per Sq. feet, total sum of Rs. 60 + 45 = 105 per Sq. feet by holding that the subject lands are abutting National Highway.
The respondent No.3 in its order enhanced the compensation at Rs.105/- per Sq. feet from Rs. 9.18/- per Sq. feet and awarded additional compensation of Rs.95.82/- per Sq. feet.
The said enhancement has been challenged by the petitioner in this petition.

The grievance of the petitioner is that the respondent No.3 without considering the relevant provisions of NHA Act and also without considering the guidance value or market value of the property as on the date of Preliminary Notification enhanced the compensation by relying on the guidance value of the year 2004 published vide notification bearing No. CVC/RGN/3/2003-04 dated 21.07.2004 and the said document is not part of arbitration proceedings.
The petitioner also claimed that the Preliminary Notification dated 05.12.2002.

As such, the respondent No. 3 ought to have considered the market value of the land of the year 2002 and not of the year 2004 as the aforesaid notification relied by the Arbitrator came to effect from 2004 i.e., after lapse of more than a year from the date of publication of Preliminary Notification.
Accordingly claimed that the said enhancement cannot be accepted.
It is true that as per the NH Act, the market value of the land as on the date of Preliminary Notification has to be considered.

.11. The petitioner also claimed that whatever the document relied by the respondent No.3 for enhancing the compensation is not A.P. No.97/2021 brought to the notice of the petitioner before passing the award/judgment.
Accordingly, claimed that such award is liable to be set aside as per Section 24 of National Highways Authority Act.
In this context, the petitioner relied on the decision reported in (2019) 15 SCC 131 in a case of Ssangyong Engineering and Construction Company Limited Vs. National Highways Authority of India.

entities.text: Ssangyong Engineering and Construction Company Limited Vs. National Highways Authority of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is true that in the said decision, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that whatever the document relied by the Arbitrator shall be brought to the notice of the parties, so that the parties can make submission or give a rebuttal evidence about such documents.
However, in the case on hand, such notification is not found in the record received from the Arbitrator.
In the case on hand, the Arbitrator has enhanced compensation to tune of 75%.
There is no reasoning for enhancement of 75% of the compensation amount.
It is simply stated that 75% compensation has been enhanced.
It is well settled principle of law that discretion must be used judiciously and not arbitrarily.
Whatever the enhancement has been granted by the Arbitrator,
certainly
effect the State or State Exchequer.
Hence, Arbitrator shall give reasons for enhancement of the compensation.

As already stated above, the Arbitrator / respondent No. 3 has not A.P.
No.97/2021 given any explanation for enhancement of 75%.
Hence such enhancement cannot be accepted.

In the case on hand, though the respondent No.1 to 4 served with the notice not chosen to appear before the court to resist the case of the petitioner or to support the award passed by the respondent No.3.
Absolutely there is no material placed before the court to disbelieve the petitioner case or to substantiate the award passed by the respondent No.3.
Hence, this Court is of the humble opinion that the petitioner has made out sufficient grounds to intervene with the award passed by the Arbitrator and the award is liable to be set aside.
Accordingly, the point No. 1 is held in the affirmative.
.13. Point No.2:
In view of my above finding, I proceed to pass the following.
ORDER Petition is allowed.

Consequently, the award passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No.3 in case No. LAQ / ARB / NH-7 / CR / 14 / 2010-11 dated A.P. No.97/2021 measuring 1100 Sq. Meters (11 guntas) equivalent to 11836 Sq. feet of Sonnappanahalli village is set aside.
